items.mnemonic: A RABBIT hops along the harbor with a SHELL full of coins, swapping carrots for silk on every dock — that busy swapping is TRADE.
The professor stands before a LATTICE of scribbled notes and begins to SAY them aloud, row by row, to a hall of students — a LECTURE.
Beside the BED a SAMURAI lays out his CLOTHES piece by piece, ties every cord and stands fully dressed, every detail of his ATTIRE.
An OLD storyteller sits in the SUN and begins to SAY the names of every village, island and clan he has visited — all of them so VARIOUS.
On stage a TIGER and a PIG cross a wooden SWORD, roaring and squealing while the audience gasps — pure DRAMA.
WATER so wide you hammer a NAIL into the bank and shout from the MOUTH of the valley to be heard on the far side — a great RIVER.
On the BOAT the captain lifts the LID off a chest, spreads a chart across the TABLE and plots the course — ready to NAVIGATE.
GOLD with one dark STROKE through it, and the HUSBAND swings his hammer at the anvil — not gold at all, but IRON.
One STROKE of chalk on the board, the SUN pouring through the window, and little LEGS racing off to the playground — a CHILD.
Between one TREE and another TREE stands an ALTAR with a rope stretched across the path: sacred ground, no entry — PROHIBIT.
A CLAW presses into warm red wax; when it lifts, a stamped mark is left behind — a SEAL.
On the ROAD a signpost has been planted UPSIDE DOWN, so every traveler sets off the wrong way — REVERSE.
A HAND pushes a parcel BOUND UP in string through the window FRAME, and LEGS run off with a BIG box in return — an EXCHANGE.
A bent traveler leaning on a stick, still walking the same road he set out on years ago — it has been a LONG TIME.
An ARROW no longer than a BEAN: you can flick it across the table but never shoot it — SHORT.
The SUN bakes the fields for TWENTY days, then EIGHT days of WATER crash down in a storm that rips the roofs off barns — VIOLENCE.
Roll a SCROLL tight, stand it on its edge under the CAR and watch it spin — a perfect WHEEL.
The DIVINATION crack in the turtle shell is read aloud by a MOUTH that announces your future — FORTUNE-TELLING.
A TREE sapling, then TEN more; the gardener's EYE checks each row while a FISHHOOK on a string marks the straight line — time to PLANT.
WATER so clear that it shows the BLUE sky in every ripple — PURE.
A PERSON told to STAND up and open the MOUTH wide gets a second helping — twice the portion, DOUBLE.
Spread the EARTH, WRAP it in a cloth and press until TWO uneven mounds are level and EQUAL.
A PERSON hears the SOUND of coins pouring in and the HEART races: more than you could count in a lifetime, a HUNDRED MILLION.
A CLIFF leaning its whole weight onto the EARTH below, squeezing it flat — PRESSURE.
GRASS clipped into the shape of a CLOUD by a patient gardener's shears — the skill of ART.
A NET of corridors, an OLD clerk at every desk, the SUN gleaming off stamped papers — the GOVERNMENT OFFICE.
A PERSON reaches up like a bolt of LIGHTNING shooting from the ground to the sky — a long STRETCH.
A PERSON waits at a kiosk with a LID on top, a MOUTH-sized window, a COVER over the bench and a NAIL holding the timetable — here the bus will STOP.
FIRE meets the heat of the SUN for TWENTY seconds, EIGHT drops of WATER hit the pan, and the whole thing blows up — EXPLODE.
From the HILL you see EARTH, then EIGHT fields more, then EARTH again to the horizon with no sea in sight — solid LAND.
WATER wrinkles its SKIN as the wind brushes over it — a WAVE.
TWENTY turns of CLOTH wound around the waist beneath a COVER of silk — the BELT.
One extra STROKE of the brush where you should STOP, and the line keeps going as you STRETCH it across the page — EXTEND.
Inside an ENCLOSURE sit TEN stones and a MOUTH that refuses to open: nothing moves, nothing gives — HARD.
A SHELL of coins and a SWORD laid side by side on the magistrate's desk: pay the fine or answer to the law — the RULE.
A TONGUE babbling nonsense while a FISHHOOK tangles every line in the boat — DISORDER.
A ROW of houses, every one lit by the same SUN, nothing special about any of them — UNIVERSAL.
Dip a SWORD into the WATER, mark the wet line and count SHELL coins along it to see how deep it goes — MEASURE.
A CURVE of baskets heaped so high with every BEAN of the harvest that they spill over — ABUNDANT.
Under a CLIFF, the SUN warms a CHILD wrapped in a quilt so padded it stands up by itself — THICK.
Count every TOOTH a PERSON has left, ONE by ONE, the way a vet reads a bird's BEAK, and you can tell their AGE.
An ENCLOSURE of stones built around the village WELL so that nobody falls in — SURROUND.
Under a LID of square caps, one PERSON after another PERSON files past, TEN at a time, to collect a diploma — GRADUATE.
Cross the RICE FIELD on WALKING LEGS and tell the farmer with one word from your MOUTH instead of ten — ABBREVIATE.
FINISH the oath, bow THREE times and pour the WATER to seal it: the request is accepted — CONSENT.
The RIVER carries each HEAD of lettuce downstream one behind the other, never jumping the queue — ORDER.
Pull a THREAD toward the EAST, again and again at dawn, until the motion is perfect — PRACTICE.
A CAR so small your RIGHT HAND lifts it clear of the EARTH — LIGHT.
A child's figure with its arms tucked away, the last stroke hooked down and done — FINISH.
A LEAN-TO with a single NAIL for the official notice board: the humblest GOVERNMENT OFFICE.
Pile up EARTH high enough and it will BECOME a fortress with white walls and a stone moat — a CASTLE.
Worry runs like a SKEWER through the HEART and will not come out — AFFLICTED.
A CORPSE-shaped roof, then HORNS, then a RICE FIELD, then the SUN, stacked one on top of another like the floors of a tower — each a LAYER.
A wooden SLAB carried down from the CLIFF, carved by a steady RIGHT HAND and inked for printing — an EDITION.
A PERSON raises ONE finger and every BEAK in the flock snaps shut: everyone obeys — an ORDER.
The curved HORN of a bull, ridged and sharp, which gives every corner its sharp ANGLE.
A THREAD trails behind WALKING LEGS and winds around a MOUTH calling for help — ENTANGLE.
A HAND slips, a MOUTH gasps, and the SHELL of coins rolls into the drain — a LOSS.
On the GRASS under the SUN a BIG banner calls for anyone with POWER to join the team — RECRUIT.
Under the LID of the collar a whole VILLAGE could hide in the lining of the CLOTHES — the side nobody sees, the BACK.
A PERSON who keeps a PRIVATE calm that no noise can shake, seated with half-closed eyes — a BUDDHA.
THREAD spun from the first SPROUT of the season and sold for a SHELL of coins: the year's record of ACHIEVEMENT.
BAMBOO scaffolding, a carpenter's CRAFT, a SAIL for the roof and a TREE for the beams — BUILD.
A PERSON trades a SPOON for a SHELL at the market stall; everything laid out on the table is GOODS.
Pour WATER into the pot, let the SUN warm it, then COMPARE the swirling colors as they blend — MIX.
The SUN climbs one STROKE higher each minute, lifted from below the horizon by TWO HANDS — RISE.
A single drop falling into a dish, the mark still sitting on the rim — BLOOD.
WATER left in a DISH under the SUN all afternoon is pleasantly WARM.
GRAIN ripens and a CHILD grows a little taller, one turn of the year at a time — a SEASON.
Water branching into streams that keep flowing long after everyone who saw them is gone — ETERNITY.
In the GRASS an OLD writer sits in the SUN, brush in hand, signing the book she wrote — the AUTHOR.
What people SAY about the SAMURAI's HEART, printed every week for all to read — a MAGAZINE.
A LEAN-TO just big enough to park the CAR and stack the boxes — a WAREHOUSE.
Pages pinned to a CLOTHESLINE to dry, then trimmed with a SWORD and bound — PUBLISH.
A PERSON carves a figure BOUND UP in cloth, with a MOUTH and the round belly of a PIG, until it looks exactly like the model — an IMAGE.
GRAIN warming in the SUN gives off the sweet smell of fresh bread — FRAGRANCE.
EARTH piled against a CLIFF so steeply that your RIGHT HAND grabs for a rail as you climb — a SLOPE.
Inside the LEAN-TO the CLAN digs down to ONE last flat stone and can go no deeper — the BOTTOM.
An ARM unrolls a bolt of fabric across the counter, yard after yard — CLOTH.
A hand-sized plot of earth set aside for prayer, a bell ringing across it in the morning mist — the TEMPLE.
A ROOF so vast it needs TWO beams and a HOOK to hold the stars in place — the UNIVERSE.
A carpenter's square so large that only a GIANT could hold it — GIANT.
RAIN hammers down and a SCALLOP on the seabed snaps shut as the ground shudders — a QUAKE.
A CROSS stitched by a tired ARM onto the last scrap of CLOTH: a rare thing, held onto with HOPE.
A HORN brushes against an INSECT and both of them jump — TOUCH.
A PERSON wrapped tightly in borrowed CLOTHES, leaning on the lender for everything — RELY.
On BAMBOO slips the clerk notes who owns each PLOW, TWENTY families a day, working until the SUN sets — the REGISTER.
WATER with TWO oily streaks and a rusty HOOK dragged through it — DIRTY.
